project.name: midas-touch
project.description: A Python pipeline for financial/tax data: ingests/generates finance data, builds embedding training datasets (synthetic query generation, hard-negative mining), trains embedding models, and serves a RAG recommender agent backed by PostgreSQL.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the embedding pipeline that re-exports config, dataset builder, document parser, hard-negative miner, pipeline, and query synthesizer public symbols.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__ acting as a public API aggregator.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central dataclass-based configuration for the embedding pipeline, defining NIM client, teacher model, hard-negative mining, query synthesis, LoRA, training, paths, and prompt templates plus a composite PipelineConfig with validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Nested frozen/standard dataclasses composed into a single PipelineConfig aggregate.

nodes.name: dataset_builder.py
nodes.summary: Assembles query/positive/hard-negative triplets, splits them into train/eval sets, and handles JSONL serialization plus dataset statistics for embedding fine-tuning.

nodes.name: document_parser.py
nodes.summary: Parses PDF, Markdown, and text financial documents into cleaned passages using a recursive financial-aware chunker with configurable size and overlap.

nodes.name: hard_negative_miner.py
nodes.summary: Mines hard negative passages for queries using a teacher SentenceTransformer embedder and an NV-Retriever margin filter, with embedding caching and mining statistics.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses numpy similarity matrices and torch.no_grad encoding for teacher-model inference.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the end-to-end embedding dataset pipeline across passage loading, query synthesis, hard-negative mining, and triplet assembly stages with checkpointing and optional database persistence.

nodes.name: query_synthesizer.py
nodes.summary: Generates synthetic search queries from passages via an async NVIDIA NIM LLM client, with concurrency control, query validation, JSON extraction, and filtering.
nodes.languageNotes: Async/await with httpx.AsyncClient, semaphore-bounded concurrency, and async context managers.

nodes.name: train.py
nodes.summary: Fine-tunes a student SentenceTransformer model on assembled triplets using MarginMSE or MultipleNegativesRanking loss with optional LoRA adapters and IR evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps sentence-transformers Trainer with PEFT LoRA application.

nodes.name: test_document_parser.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests validating the FinancialChunker splitting behavior and the DocumentParser text/markdown parsing path.

nodes.name: HardNegativeConfig

nodes.name: LoraConfig

nodes.name: TrainingConfig

nodes.name: PathConfig

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Midas Touch is: a Python financial/tax pipeline that fine-tunes embeddings and powers a recommendation agent, backed by PostgreSQL with pgvector. The document walks through the uv-based environment setup, the directory layout separating raw SQL schema, reusable DB connectors, and runnable scripts, and the Alembic migration workflow. Read this first to get the roadmap before diving into code.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml is the modern Python project manifest. Here it is uv-managed: uv reads the [project] dependencies to build a locked, reproducible virtual environment, replacing requirements.txt.

tour.title: The Data Model
tour.description: Everything in the project rests on the SQLAlchemy ORM models, the highest fan-out file in the graph. It defines every table in the PostgreSQL/pgvector schema: investor Users and Portfolios, TaxRules and MarketSnapshots, plus the embedding tables (NewsEmbedding, StrategyDoc, PersonaEmbedding) that carry 1024-dimensional vectors. These classes are the shared vocabulary that the connectors, pipelines, and agent all speak.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy ORM models map Python classes to database tables via a declarative Base. The pgvector Vector column type stores embeddings natively so similarity search runs inside the database.

tour.title: The SQL Schema and Seeds
tour.description: Building on the ORM models from Step 2, the raw SQL schema is the ground truth the database is provisioned from. It declares the same users, portfolios, tax_rules and market tables, plus the vector tables whose embedding columns are HNSW-indexed for fast semantic search. The tax-rule seed file loads the baseline reference rows the recommender later relies on.
tour.languageLesson: An HNSW index (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) makes approximate nearest-neighbor search over pgvector columns fast, trading a small amount of recall for large speed gains on similarity queries.

tour.title: Database Connectors
tour.description: The connector module is the most depended-upon piece of plumbing in the project, tying for highest fan-in. It centralizes the PostgreSQL connection and cursor helpers and exposes upsert/query functions for users, market snapshots, tax rules, persona similarity search, and the embedding-pipeline tables. The Supabase connector reuses the same shared cursor to add vector-search helpers for news, strategy docs, and macro indicators.

tour.title: Data Ingestion Pipelines
tour.description: With the data model and connectors in place, these modules fill the database. fetch_market_data pulls from yfinance, FRED, and ECOS via a MarketDataPipeline orchestrator, while generate_finance_data uses an LLM to synthesize investor profiles from CSV rows and bulk-upserts them. export_csv prepares the persona source data that downstream embedding steps consume.

tour.title: Embedding Pipeline Configuration
tour.description: Now we reach the heart of the project. config.py is the most depended-upon file in the embedding pipeline, a set of dataclasses defining the NIM client, teacher model, hard-negative mining, query synthesis, LoRA, training, and paths, composed into one validated PipelineConfig. Every pipeline stage imports it, so understanding these knobs unlocks the rest.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses generate boilerplate (init, repr, eq) from typed field declarations, making them ideal for layered configuration objects that are validated once and passed by reference.

tour.title: From Documents to Queries
tour.description: The first two pipeline stages turn raw text into training signal. document_parser chunks PDF, Markdown, and text financial documents into clean passages with a financial-aware recursive splitter, and query_synthesizer asks an async NVIDIA NIM LLM to generate realistic search queries for each passage, with concurrency control and validation. Together they produce the (query, positive passage) pairs that anchor the dataset.
tour.languageLesson: Python async/await with bounded concurrency (e.g. a semaphore) lets the query synthesizer fire many LLM calls in flight at once while capping load on the NIM endpoint.

tour.title: Hard Negatives and Dataset Assembly
tour.description: Building on the queries from Step 7, hard_negative_miner uses a teacher SentenceTransformer plus an NV-Retriever margin filter to find tricky negative passages that are similar but wrong, with embedding caching for speed. dataset_builder then assembles query/positive/hard-negative triplets, splits them into train/eval, and serializes JSONL. These are the contrastive examples that make the fine-tuned model discriminative.

tour.title: Pipeline Orchestration and Training
tour.description: pipeline.py is the conductor that runs passage loading, query synthesis, hard-negative mining, and triplet assembly end-to-end with checkpointing and optional database persistence into the emb_ tables. train.py then fine-tunes a student SentenceTransformer on the assembled triplets using MarginMSE or MultipleNegativesRanking loss, optionally with LoRA adapters, evaluated by IR metrics. This is where the embedding model is actually produced.
tour.languageLesson: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) freezes the base model and trains small adapter matrices, cutting the trainable parameter count by orders of magnitude so a large embedding model can be fine-tuned cheaply.

tour.title: The RAG Recommender Agent
tour.description: This is the payoff that ties the whole system together. The MidasAdviser agent embeds a user's profile, retrieves similar 'twin' personas, applicable tax rules, and market snapshots from PostgreSQL using the connectors from Step 4 and the vectors produced by the embedding pipeline, then asks an LLM for a tailored financial recommendation. The test suite exercises both the DB helpers and the full recommendation flow.

tour.title: Runnable Entry Points
tour.description: These CLI scripts are how a user actually drives the system. run_agent launches the MidasAdviser in one-shot or interactive questionnaire mode, run_market_pipeline and run_persona_pipeline trigger ingestion and persona-embedding population, and migrate_data backfills the PostgreSQL target from the legacy Azure SQL and Supabase sources. Start here when you want to run something.

tour.title: Infrastructure and Migrations
tour.description: Finally, the operational layer. docker-compose provisions a single PostgreSQL 16 container with a persistent volume, while db_init.sh boots it and exposes it via an ngrok tunnel. Alembic's env.py and the versioned migration files (the consolidated initial schema plus the embedding-pipeline tables) keep the live database in sync with the ORM models from Step 2 as they evolve.
tour.languageLesson: Alembic migrations version the database schema: each file has an upgrade and downgrade, chained by revision IDs, so the database can move forward or back in lockstep with the SQLAlchemy models.
